title: Science Basics
subject: science
year_note: Age hint 11. Water's formula, what the Sun is and how a vaccine works are Levels 3 to 4 science; the band is a little wider than the age hint on both sides because the bank is a general one.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: Each water molecule is two hydrogen atoms joined to one oxygen atom.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury whips around the Sun in just 88 Earth days.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because its surface is covered in rusty iron oxide dust.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight to make their food.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The oxygen we breathe mostly comes from plants and ocean algae.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The air is about 78 percent nitrogen and only 21 percent oxygen.

questions.prompt: What force pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity is why dropped things fall and why the Moon stays in orbit.

questions.prompt: What is the centre of an atom called?
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the protons and neutrons, with electrons whizzing around it.

questions.prompt: What electric charge does an electron have?
questions.explanation: Electrons are negative, protons are positive, neutrons are neutral.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol O?
questions.explanation: O for oxygen, the gas your body needs every second.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin word for iron.

questions.prompt: Which element has the chemical symbol Au?
questions.explanation: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.prompt: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, lower up a mountain.

questions.prompt: At what temperature does fresh water freeze?
questions.explanation: Zero degrees Celsius was actually defined from water's freezing point.

questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
questions.explanation: Your heart beats about 100,000 times every day.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Skin counts as an organ, and it is by far the biggest one you have.

questions.prompt: How many bones does an adult human have?
questions.explanation: Babies start with around 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow.

questions.prompt: Which of these do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
questions.explanation: The stiff cell wall helps plants stand up without a skeleton.

questions.prompt: What does DNA stand for?
questions.explanation: DNA is the molecule that carries the instructions for building you.

questions.prompt: What kind of object is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is an ordinary star that just happens to be very close to us.

questions.prompt: About how long does the Moon take to orbit the Earth?
questions.explanation: One trip around Earth takes the Moon about 27 days.

questions.prompt: Sound travels fastest through which of these?
questions.explanation: Particles in a solid are packed tightly, so vibrations pass along quickly.

questions.prompt: Why do you see lightning before you hear the thunder?
choices: Light travels much faster than sound
Your eyes react faster than your ears
questions.explanation: Light reaches you almost instantly, while sound takes about 3 seconds per kilometre.

questions.prompt: Solar panels turn sunlight into what?
questions.explanation: Solar cells turn light energy straight into electrical energy.

questions.prompt: What are the three common states of matter?
questions.explanation: Most everyday stuff is a solid, a liquid or a gas, and plasma makes a fourth.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a liquid turns into a gas?
questions.explanation: Puddles disappear on a sunny day because the water evaporates.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a gas turns into a liquid?
questions.explanation: Water droplets on a cold window are condensation from the air.

questions.prompt: An animal that eats only plants is called what?
questions.explanation: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat meat, omnivores eat both.

questions.prompt: A whale is which kind of animal?
questions.explanation: Whales breathe air and feed their babies milk, so they are mammals.

questions.prompt: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.explanation: Six legs is the insect rule; spiders have eight, so they are not insects.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explanation: Eight legs makes spiders arachnids, not insects.

questions.prompt: How long does Earth take to spin once on its axis?
questions.explanation: One full spin gives us one day and one night.

questions.prompt: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun?
questions.explanation: One full orbit is one year, which is why a year has about 365 days.

questions.prompt: On the pH scale, what does a value of 7 mean?
questions.explanation: Pure water sits at pH 7, right in the middle of the scale.

questions.prompt: What happens when you push the north poles of two magnets together?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel and opposite poles attract.

questions.prompt: Which of these materials conducts electricity well?
questions.explanation: That is why electrical wires are usually made of copper.

questions.prompt: Which green pigment lets plants capture light energy?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is what makes leaves look green.

questions.prompt: What is the scientific unit of force?
questions.explanation: It is named after Isaac Newton, who described how forces work.

questions.prompt: How does a vaccine protect you?
choices: It makes your blood too thick for germs
It kills every germ in your body
It teaches your immune system to recognise a germ
questions.explanation: After a vaccine, your immune system remembers the germ and fights it fast.
